findings.title: Public group members page is silently capped at 50
findings.body: Group.findMembers always requests limit 50 (the model default) and offset 0, and the public group members route only calls findMembers() with no pager. group/members.hbs iterates members and has no next/previous controls (those exist only on the admin group screen). GroupsController#members now applies that limit to every group and no longer returns the full list: non-automatic groups previously returned every member, and automatic groups defaulted to 200. Any group with more than 50 members now shows only the first page, with no indication the list is incomplete and no way to see the rest.

findings.title: Page count is one too high when size is a multiple of the page size
findings.body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (including exactly 50, the default page size) that yields an extra page: 50 members render as 1/2, 100 as 3 pages, and so on. showingLast compares currentPage to that inflated total, so Next stays enabled on the last real page. next() then sets offset to user_count, findMembers returns an empty slice, and the admin sees a blank extra page of members.

findings.title: Creating a group ignores the selected alias level
findings.body: create sets name and visible but never assigns alias_level, while update in the same controller does (params[:alias_level].to_i when present). The admin form shows the alias-level combo box for new groups (it is outside the {{#if id}} block), and Group.asJSON sends alias_level on POST /admin/groups. The chosen level is discarded and the row keeps the default (0 / nobody). The client model still holds the unsaved value, so the dropdown looks correct until reload, when it reverts. The create spec only checks name stripping, so this is untested.

findings.title: Update forces visible to false when the param is omitted
findings.body: update sets group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" unconditionally, unlike alias_level and name which are applied only when present. Any PUT or PATCH that does not include visible=true therefore hides the group and still returns 200. resources :groups still routes PATCH to update, and the removed update_patch path used to change membership without touching visible. A leftover PATCH {changes: {add: ...}} (old admin JS or an API client) now adds nobody and silently sets visible to false. Partial updates that only rename the group do the same.

findings.title: Adding members does not trim names and can commit a partial update
findings.body: add_members splits usernames on commas and looks each piece up with User.find_by_username without stripping. A normal typed value such as "alice, bob" looks up " bob", matches nobody, and is skipped. Unknown names are ignored and the action still returns success, so the admin UI reloads an unchanged list and cannot tell the user who was not added. group.add on an already-persisted group inserts the join row immediately, and the loop is not wrapped in a transaction: if a later name raises (duplicate membership / RecordNotUnique), earlier adds stay committed while the request 500s. The new spec only posts already-clean comma-separated names, so none of this is covered.

findings.title: Member removal bypasses Group#remove and 404s if already gone
findings.body: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) instead of Group#remove, which the previous membership path used. Passing an id makes ActiveRecord find the user inside the association first, so a user who is not currently a member raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound (404) rather than succeeding as a no-op. For a has_many :through with no :dependent option, delete then delete_alls join rows and skips GroupUser destroy callbacks. Adds go through group.add, which is what keeps user_count in sync (the index spec expects user_count == 1 after add). Removals can therefore leave user_count, titles, or primary-group side effects stale. The new spec only asserts users.count after a successful delete, so that drift would still pass. The admin client also has no error handler on this request, so a 404 leaves the member on screen with no message.

findings.title: Members endpoint does not bound limit or offset
findings.body: limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset = params[:offset].to_i are passed straight into the query. There is no maximum, so anyone who can see a group (including anonymous users, for a visible automatic group such as trust_level_0) can pass limit=1000000 and force the process to load and serialize the entire membership. Negative values are also accepted: PostgreSQL rejects LIMIT -1 and OFFSET -1, so a request like limit=-1 returns 500. A zero limit is echoed back to the admin client, which then divides by zero in totalPages and renders a broken pager.

findings.title: Out-of-range member offsets are echoed back as a blank page
findings.body: offset is taken from params with to_i and returned unchanged in meta.offset, even when it is past the end of the list. After the admin removes the last member on a page, Group.removeMember calls findMembers without moving offset backward. The client clamp uses the pre-request user_count (still the old total), so it still requests the old offset. The server, now with fewer users, returns an empty members array and the same offset; the client stores that offset. The UI sits on a blank page (and, with the off-by-one page count, may show 2/2 for a list that now fits on one page) until the admin clicks Previous. Negative offsets are likewise not corrected and make PostgreSQL raise.

findings.title: Enter in the group form activates Add instead of Save
findings.body: The new form wraps the name field, the user selector, and the action buttons, but none of the buttons set type="button" and the form has no submit handler. In HTML the default button type is submit, and pressing Enter in a text field synthetically clicks the first submit button in the form. Once the group has an id, that button is Add, not Save. Enter in the name field therefore runs addMembers (re-adding whatever is still in the username box) and does not save the name, visibility, or alias level. If Ember's action helper does not preventDefault, the form also does a GET navigation of the current admin URL and discards the in-page state. On a new group the first button is Save, so Enter behaves differently before and after the first save.

findings.title: Add and remove failures are silent and the username field is never cleared
findings.body: addMembers posts the usernames and, on success, does not clear the field (the TODO on the previous line). removeMember and addMembers both ignore rejected promises. A 422 (automatic group), 404 (member already gone), 500 (duplicate add), or network error closes the confirm dialog or clicks Add and then changes nothing on screen, so the admin cannot tell failure from a no-op. Because the field stays filled, a second click resubmits the same names; if Group#add raises on a duplicate, that second click 500s. Newly added users are also only reloaded on the current offset, so someone who sorts onto another page never appears in the list even though the request succeeded.

findings.title: Username box is not reset when switching groups
findings.body: Admin group controllers are Ember singletons. setupController replaces the model and reloads members but does not clear controller.usernames. The add-members field is bound to that controller property, and addMembers never clears it after a successful add either. Navigating from group A to group B leaves A's pending (or just-added) usernames in the box; clicking Add then PUTs those names onto group B. Offset is stored on the group model so it does not leak, but usernames were left on the shared controller when membership was split out of the save payload.

findings.title: Member reloads use the unsaved name from the text field
findings.body: findMembers builds GET /groups/<name>/members.json from this.get('name'), and the admin name input is two-way bound to that property. Editing the name and then paging, adding, or removing a member fetches (or fails to fetch) the unsaved name before Save. Remove itself uses the numeric id and can succeed, but the follow-up findMembers 404s, so the list never refreshes and the removed user stays on screen. The name is also interpolated without encodeURIComponent, so a value that still contains spaces produces a broken URL. Pagination has already written the new offset before the request, so a failed reload leaves the page indicator and the member list out of sync.

findings.title: Client keeps the unstripped name after create
findings.body: create() only copies resp.basic_group.id from the POST response. The server strips the name before save and returns the stored name on BasicGroupSerializer, but the in-memory group keeps whatever was typed, including leading or trailing spaces. showGroup then navigates with that unsaved name, so a refresh looks the group up by the spaced name, misses the record named "bob", and the admin route sends the user back to the index. A later Save sends the spaced name to update, which assigns params[:name] with no strip (create strips, update does not). That either fails name-format validation or writes the spaces back over the cleaned name.

findings.title: GET group members no longer returns a bare array
findings.body: GroupsController#members used to render_serialized an array of GroupUserSerializer objects. It now returns {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}. The in-repo Group.findMembers client was updated, but any other caller — plugins, API scripts, or a browser still running the previous JS that did result.map(...) — will throw because the top-level JSON is an object. The reverse is also true during a rolling deploy: new JS expects result.members and result.meta and crashes on the old array. There is no versioned path or compatibility shim, and no spec locks the new contract.

findings.title: Overlapping member-page requests can land on the wrong page
findings.body: next and previous write offset and call findMembers immediately, and the pager links are not disabled while a request is in flight. Two quick clicks start two GETs; findMembers applies whichever response arrives last via setProperties, including that response's offset. A slower response for the previous page overwrites a later click, so the list and the page indicator show a page the admin already left. Nothing ignores a stale response.

findings.title: Automatic-group removal spec uses PUT, and the public members API is untested
findings.body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route and the UI use DELETE (the success example in the same context correctly uses DELETE). Controller specs invoke the action directly, so this still hits remove_member and does not prove the DELETE route, the :group_id param, or that PUT /members is add_members. Separately, GroupsController#members was rewritten to a paginated {members, meta} payload and no spec in this pull request covers the new shape, limit/offset bounds, or the regression that non-automatic groups are no longer returned in full.
